_meta.purpose: Canonical per-country structural overlay for the FoodShield frontend. index.html remains a fallback only; this file is the preferred source for baseline structural metrics and trade snapshots.

quality_flags.sourced: Verified against a public dataset; source_url + as_of populated.
quality_flags.partial: Uses real source lineage but the audit trail is incomplete or composite; basis/unit metadata is present, but treat with caution.
quality_flags.legacy_curated: Hand-authored heritage value, not yet re-verified. Treated as draft.
quality_flags.legacy_import_dependency: Heritage value originally meant 'fraction of consumption imported' (0-100), NOT the caloric-share definition the field name now implies. Mis-display would be misleading; UI should treat as import-dependency only until replaced by FBS-sourced caloric share.
quality_flags.heritage: Inherited historical value with no current direct-source audit trail.
quality_flags.modeled: Computed from sourced inputs or explicit structural assumptions.
quality_flags.manual: Hand-maintained snapshot from an annual or static public release.

source_priority: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets caloric shares (w/r/m) — when present
FAOSTAT Trade Crops & Livestock net food balance (net) — when present
Embedded legacy fallback extracted from index.html
notes: Caloric shares (w/r/m) come from FAOSTAT FBS; net food trade from FAOSTAT TCL.
Trade-facing fields carry explicit basis/unit metadata via trade_schema.py so value-ranked and quantity-ranked rows are not silently mixed.
Rows labeled partial are derived from real source lineage but are not yet directly auditable from a single public extract.
Food-only UI menus may be normalized at render time; canonical raw structural values remain stored here.
The frontend supports both the historical top-level countries schema and this v20.6 envelope schema for safe rollout.

econ_access.source: WDI (reserves, debt-service) + UNDP HDI (income) + FX pipeline
econ_access.method: Economic Access fragility: blend of FX 12m depreciation, reserves-in-months (convex cliff), debt-service %% of exports, and GNI per capita (log). No CPI (price stress stays in Food Inflation).

grain_buffer.method: Grain Reserve Buffer fragility: 100 = thin stocks-to-use (ending stocks / consumption across staples), 0 = ample cushion. Source: USDA PSD.

import_dep.source: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (cereal import dependency ratio)
import_dep.method: Sum of import quantity (element 5611) divided by sum of domestic supply quantity (element 5301) across wheat, rice and maize, expressed 0-100. FAO's cereal import dependency ratio.

supplier_conc.method: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of import shares (sum of squared shares), renormalised over the observed top-5 partners and expressed 0-100. Chosen over top-3 share because top-3 cannot separate 60/20/10 from 34/33/33 — both read 90, and they are very different exposures.

econ_access.source: WDI (reserves, debt-service) + UNDP HDI (income) + FX pipeline
econ_access.method: Economic Access fragility: blend of FX 12m depreciation, reserves-in-months (convex cliff), debt-service %% of exports, and GNI per capita (log). No CPI (price stress stays in Food Inflation).

grain_buffer.method: Grain Reserve Buffer fragility: 100 = thin stocks-to-use (ending stocks / consumption across staples), 0 = ample cushion. Source: USDA PSD.

import_dep.source: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (cereal import dependency ratio)
import_dep.method: Sum of import quantity (element 5611) divided by sum of domestic supply quantity (element 5301) across wheat, rice and maize, expressed 0-100. FAO's cereal import dependency ratio.

supplier_conc.method: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of import shares (sum of squared shares), renormalised over the observed top-5 partners and expressed 0-100. Chosen over top-3 share because top-3 cannot separate 60/20/10 from 34/33/33 — both read 90, and they are very different exposures.

prod_trend.source: FAOSTAT Production Indices (Gross Production Index, Food, 2014-2016 = 100)
prod_trend.method: OLS slope of the gross food production index over 2015-2024, expressed as average annual % change against the window mean, then mapped to 0-100 fragility where falling production scores high (-3%/yr -> 100, flat -> 50, +3%/yr -> 0).

c_heritage.method: The original hand-authored 9-component vector, pinned so that sourced-vs-heritage blending stays idempotent across nightly rebuilds. This is an AUTHORING date, not a data vintage — that is the whole reason these components are being replaced.

fdrs.method: FDRS v2 (9-component weighted composite + import×economic-access amplifier). See methodology.
fdrs.note: Computed by the FDRS v2 formula from the component vector. Some components are sourced, some still legacy; displayed score adds live supply-chain exposure + nowcast.

econ_access.source: WDI (reserves, debt-service) + UNDP HDI (income) + FX pipeline
econ_access.method: Economic Access fragility: blend of FX 12m depreciation, reserves-in-months (convex cliff), debt-service %% of exports, and GNI per capita (log). No CPI (price stress stays in Food Inflation).

grain_buffer.method: Grain Reserve Buffer fragility: 100 = thin stocks-to-use (ending stocks / consumption across staples), 0 = ample cushion. Source: USDA PSD.

import_dep.source: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (cereal import dependency ratio)
import_dep.method: Sum of import quantity (element 5611) divided by sum of domestic supply quantity (element 5301) across wheat, rice and maize, expressed 0-100. FAO's cereal import dependency ratio.

supplier_conc.method: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of import shares (sum of squared shares), renormalised over the observed top-5 partners and expressed 0-100. Chosen over top-3 share because top-3 cannot separate 60/20/10 from 34/33/33 — both read 90, and they are very different exposures.

prod_trend.source: FAOSTAT Production Indices (Gross Production Index, Food, 2014-2016 = 100)
prod_trend.method: OLS slope of the gross food production index over 2015-2024, expressed as average annual % change against the window mean, then mapped to 0-100 fragility where falling production scores high (-3%/yr -> 100, flat -> 50, +3%/yr -> 0).

c_heritage.method: The original hand-authored 9-component vector, pinned so that sourced-vs-heritage blending stays idempotent across nightly rebuilds. This is an AUTHORING date, not a data vintage — that is the whole reason these components are being replaced.

fdrs.method: FDRS v2 (9-component weighted composite + import×economic-access amplifier). See methodology.
fdrs.note: Computed by the FDRS v2 formula from the component vector. Some components are sourced, some still legacy; displayed score adds live supply-chain exposure + nowcast.

c.method: FDRS v2 structural component vector [import_dep, supplier_conc, prod_trend, food_infl, climate, conflict, supply_chain_exposure, econ_access, grain_buffer].
c.note: Stored as the canonical 9-component structural vector. The frontend may inject live supply-chain exposure and nowcast adjustments at render time; this file preserves the structural baseline plus sourced v2 components.

f2030.method: Structural 2030 FDRS projection (forward model from current components + OECD-FAO/structural trend assumptions).
f2030.note: Reclassified from legacy_curated to modeled: a forward projection, never an observed value.

w.note: Wheat share derived from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets. Direct food calories only; indirect feed conversion is excluded.

r.note: Rice share derived from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets. Direct food calories only; indirect feed conversion is excluded.

m.note: Maize share derived from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets. Direct food calories only; indirect feed conversion is excluded.

fi.source: FAOSTAT Consumer Price Indices (food CPI, yoy)
fi.method: Year-over-year food price inflation (%), latest available month.
fi.note: Sourced from live WFP / Eurostat / FAOSTAT food-price feeds, replacing the legacy embedded baseline. Updated on each data-refresh cycle.

net.method: Net food trade = Export Value - Import Value (1000 USD), aggregate 'Food Excluding Fish (CPC F1982)'. Values in millions USD.
net.note: Net agri-food trade balance from Agricultural Products, Total (FAOSTAT item 1841). Positive = net exporter, negative = net importer. Source year: 2024. Exports: 640.4 M USD; Imports: 660.0 M USD.

imports.method: Staples imported (imports_kt>0) ranked by tonnage, USDA PSD.

source_query_spec.dataset: USDA PSD Online bulk supply/demand balance

exports.method: Food staples ranked by export value, UN Comtrade 2024.

exportDests.method: Top-5 destinations of Sugar exports (largest export staple), UN Comtrade 2024.

suppliers.note: Suppliers aggregated across staples by real kt (UN Comtrade 2024 exporter-mirror): TZA 110.5 kt, ZAF 81.5 kt, AUS 69.2 kt, ZWE 8.3 kt, USA 0.0 kt. Total 270 kt across Wheat, Maize, Soybeans.

supPct.note: Suppliers aggregated across staples by real kt (UN Comtrade 2024 exporter-mirror): TZA 110.5 kt, ZAF 81.5 kt, AUS 69.2 kt, ZWE 8.3 kt, USA 0.0 kt. Total 270 kt across Wheat, Maize, Soybeans.

econ_access.source: WDI (reserves, debt-service) + UNDP HDI (income) + FX pipeline
econ_access.method: Economic Access fragility: blend of FX 12m depreciation, reserves-in-months (convex cliff), debt-service %% of exports, and GNI per capita (log). No CPI (price stress stays in Food Inflation).

grain_buffer.method: Grain Reserve Buffer fragility: 100 = thin stocks-to-use (ending stocks / consumption across staples), 0 = ample cushion. Source: USDA PSD.

import_dep.source: FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (cereal import dependency ratio)
import_dep.method: Sum of import quantity (element 5611) divided by sum of domestic supply quantity (element 5301) across wheat, rice and maize, expressed 0-100. FAO's cereal import dependency ratio.

supplier_conc.method: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of import shares (sum of squared shares), renormalised over the observed top-5 partners and expressed 0-100. Chosen over top-3 share because top-3 cannot separate 60/20/10 from 34/33/33 — both read 90, and they are very different exposures.
